module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 705

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/705](https://www.erdosproblems.com/705)
- [OD99] P. O'Donnell, High girth unit-distance graphs. PhD Dissertation, Rutgers University (1999).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos705

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open SimpleGraph

/--
Let $G$ be a finite unit distance graph in $\mamthbb{R}^2$.
Is there some $k$ such that if $G$ has girth $≥ k$, then $\chi(G) ≤ 3$?

The general case was solved by O'Donnell [OD99], who constructed finite unit distance graphs with
chromatic number $4$ and arbitrarily large girth.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos705.lean#L8323"]
theorem erdos_705:
  answer(False) ↔ ∃ k, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite →
    (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).girth ≥ k → (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).chromaticNumber ≤ 3 := by
  sorry


-- TODO: add statements for the concrete constructions in the additional material

end Erdos705

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the natural-valued SimpleGraph.girth, which equals 0 on acyclic graphs. The source describes girth ≥ k as having no cycles of length < k, a condition satisfied by acyclic graphs for every k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Acyclic graphs have chromatic number at most 2, so they satisfy the conclusion regardless of the girth hypothesis. For graphs containing a cycle, Mathlib's girth is the shortest cycle length. Thus, for every graph G and natural k, the Lean implication is equivalent to 'if every cycle has length at least k, then G is 3-colorable.' This equivalence, and the complete existential/universal right-hand-side equivalence, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the sorry-backed problem theorem; Review705.original_rhs_equiv_source depends only on standard axioms.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/705 — full statement and remarks read through the archived copy; current negative status confirmed through Jina.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_distance_graph — definitions of unit-distance and faithful unit-distance graphs.
review.notes: The source explicitly requires an edge iff the distance is 1, matching UnitDistancePlaneGraph. Its negative solution agrees with answer(False) and research solved. Empty and singleton sets, k = 0, finiteness, and small Euclidean distances were checked in Lean. The cited external proof was successfully recompiled after inlining its one-line notation utility; Erdos705.not_erdos_705 states the exact negation of the file's RHS and uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The original [OD99] dissertation could not be retrieved; its historical attribution was checked against the source page, not independently against the thesis.
